newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends firmer against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends firmer against dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed stronger against the dollar on Tuesday on the U.S. currency's overseas weakness and lack of demand from importers, dealers said.

"There was downward pressure on the dollar from the morning," said a foreign bank dealer. "The dollar's overseas weakness against the yen prompted banks to sell dollars. Also there were not many import bills."
The rupee closed at around 58.42 to the dollar, after opening unchanged at 58.60, dealers said.
The Central Bank's dollar-rupee exchange rate was unchanged, leaving buying and selling prices at 58.1848 and 59.3602.

Overnight call money rates closed at around 13 percent after rising to 16 percent in volatile trade as lenders dominated the market and banks covered positions ahead of two mid-week Buddhist holidays, dealers said.
There was pressure on call rates as banks faced extra cash withdrawals and dealers squared up ahead of holidays on Wednesday and Thursday, they added.
